price_sensitivity_method: For each item/location price change with positive old/new prices: sum completed-order units in fixed 30-day pre and post windows; response ratio=(post units - pre units)/pre units divided by (new price-old price)/old price; absolute ratio >=1 high sensitivity, >=0.5 moderate, otherwise low. Observational and confounded, not causal.
promotion_trap_method: Signal only if promo-cohort mean paid order total exceeds overall non-promo mean, while promo average estimated item contribution is lower; uncontrolled cohort, ignores customer acquisition/repeat/wastage/post-period and product substitution.

menu_classification_method.labels_follow_srs: Profit Driver, Volume Driver, Hidden Opportunity, Low Performer; explicit insufficient-history/cost exceptions

basket_method.pair_unit: distinct completed order x menu item

churn_rule.target: no orders in 90+ days as of max completed-order date; customers need >=2 completed orders

wastage_risk.target_definition: 1 when item/location total wastage cost in the next Monday-start week is >= training-only p75 (1596.2) of positive training weeks; otherwise 0
wastage_risk.prediction_point: At the start of each prediction week, prior completed weeks only; target week calendar is known.
wastage_risk.target_week_definition: Prediction row at week_start t predicts wastage aggregated during target_week=t+7 days.

feature_semantics.waste lags: prior observed weekly waste quantities/costs; zero-filled missing weeks
feature_semantics.demand lags: prior completed-order item quantities; zero-filled missing weeks
feature_semantics.calendar: target-week month and ISO week number

leakage_exclusions: wastage reason observed after the prediction point
wastage_risk.threshold_selection: Validation F1 over probability cutoffs 0.05..0.95; model selection by validation PR-AUC, then validation F1; test not used for selection.
wastage_risk.limitations: Generated synthetic data; weekly risk classification identifies association/predicted risk, not causal drivers. Burden thresholds refer to cost source units without currency definition.

recommendations: Versioned directional association candidates are served through the authenticated app; actions remain deterministic and noncausal. Acceptance/cost tracking and broader independent basket comparison are not implemented.
what_if: POST /api/what-if does bounded price, promotion, demand, inventory, preparation and removal arithmetic with stated assumptions; scenario outputs are not forecasts.

demand_baseline.target: Count of order records with order_datetime in [hour_start, hour_start + 1 hour), regardless of eventual order status.
demand_baseline.prediction_point: At the start of each UTC timestamp hour in the source data, before that hour's orders occur; restaurant-specific time zones are not provided.
demand_baseline.baseline: seasonal naive: same restaurant and hour-of-week at lag 168 hours
demand_baseline.split: same chronological untouched Spark held-out test interval
demand_baseline.feature_semantics_note: Spark training day_of_week maps Sunday=0; Python training uses pandas Monday=0. Python inference here uses its native Monday=0 convention. Metrics are same-period but feature semantics differ; this is not an exact controlled model comparison.

demand_model_comparison.weekday_semantics_note: Spark training day_of_week maps Sunday=0; Python training uses pandas Monday=0. Python inference here uses its native Monday=0 convention. Both models independently score the same underlying held-out records and target, so per-case outputs are comparable descriptively but not a controlled feature-equivalent model comparison.
